discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: moiré quantum materials
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (PNAS 2011) predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees flattens the electronic bands, so that interactions dominate kinetic energy. Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers (Nature 2018, two papers) realized this experimentally and found correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity that can be switched by gating a single device. The work turned the twist angle into a new control parameter for quantum matter. It started the field of moiré materials, which many groups worldwide have reproduced and extended: orbital ferromagnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect, generalized Wigner crystals, moiré excitons and magnetism, and most recently fractional quantum anomalous Hall states and fractional Chern insulators at zero magnetic field in twisted MoTe2 and rhombohedral graphene. Few recent discoveries have opened such a broad, tunable platform for strongly correlated and topological physics.
